title: The coordinate quotient map is an epimorphism, by the two-chart surjectivity calculation.
statement: Let k be a field, P=Proj k[x_0,x_1] with the standard grading [def-sc-p1-standard], G any O_P-module, and z an integer. With twists and coordinate multiplication as in [def-weil-pbc-proj-twisting-sheaf], the morphism (μ_0(z),μ_1(z)):G(z) ⊕ G(z) -> G(z+1) is an epimorphism.

source.place: Two-chart calculation, proof steps 1 and 2 (not an application of the parent theorem)

proof.text:
Proof: The irrelevant ideal is generated by x_0 and x_1, so D+(x_0) and
D+(x_1) cover Proj. On D+(x_i), twistMul by x_i is invertible, including
for negative twists. Restriction agrees with pullback, and pullback is
monoidal; hence G whiskered with this map is also invertible locally.
At any point choose a chart containing it. The corresponding coordinate
map is surjective on its stalk and factors through the quotient map by
the corresponding biproduct inclusion. The quotient map is therefore
surjective on this stalk. Surjectivity at every stalk implies epimorphy.
This applies to the zero module and arbitrary torsion modules without flatness.

proof_origin.place: Two-chart calculation, proof steps 1 and 2 (not an application of the parent theorem)

lean.statement:
theorem proj_coordinate_quotient_epi
    (k : Type u) [Field k]
    (G : (Proj (MvPolynomial.homogeneousSubmodule (Fin 2) k)).Modules) (z : ℤ) :
    Epi (biprod.desc
      (G ◁ Proj.twistMul z (MvPolynomial.X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k (0 : Fin 2)))
      (G ◁ Proj.twistMul z (MvPolynomial.X_mem_homogeneousSubmodule_one k (1 : Fin 2))))
